extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: Do NOT use speechManager.speak() anywhere in the game. Only use audioManager.play() for sound effects. Valid sound effects: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint. The game must teach: (1) Directions (left, right, near, far) — left and right are relative to which way we face. Near means close by, far means a long way away. Practice with classroom objects — 'the blackboard is in front, the door is on the right'. (2) Four main directions — North (N), South (S), East (E), West (W). The sun rises in the EAST and sets in the WEST. If you face the rising sun (east), your left hand points NORTH and right hand points SOUTH. North and South are opposite, East and West are opposite. A compass shows all four directions. (3) Picture maps — a map is a drawing that shows where things are. Picture maps use small drawings (icons) for buildings, roads, rivers, parks. We can locate places on a map — school, hospital, park, market, post office. Maps help us find our way. (4) Water sources — natural sources (river, pond, lake, sea, spring, rainwater), man-made sources (tap, well, hand pump, water tank, water cooler, dam). Water at home comes from taps, which is supplied from rivers, lakes, or groundwater through pipes. (5) Land and water around us — land features (mountains, hills, plains, plateaus, deserts, valleys), water features (rivers, ponds, lakes, seas, oceans, waterfalls, streams). Both land and water are parts of the Earth's surface. Misconceptions: 'sun rises in the west' (sun rises in the EAST, sets in the WEST), 'if I face east, my right is north' (facing east: left=NORTH, right=SOUTH), 'sea water is safe to drink' (sea water is salty and not safe to drink), 'a map is just a picture' (a map shows real places and where they are located, not just any picture), 'north and east are opposite' (north is opposite to south, east is opposite to west). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function DirectionsMapGame), NOT export default. Export interface DirectionsMapGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
